I am 63 years old this year, and I have been working the land since I was ten. I finished primary school, and after that I learned everything from my father and from doing it with my own two hands. My farm is 20 mu, which is a good-sized piece of land around here. I have 8 mu of wheat that I sowed last October, and I plant summer maize on that same ground after the wheat comes off in early June. The other 12 mu is for cotton. Cotton is my main crop — I have been growing it for more than 30 years, and I know every step of it.

Last year my wheat gave me about 1000 jin per mu, my maize gave about 1200 jin, and my cotton gave about 550 jin of seed cotton per mu. It was an ordinary year. This year I will do more or less the same thing, because at my age I do not try new tricks. If it worked before, I do it again.

For the wheat that is already in the ground: I sowed about 30 jin of seed per mu. I use Luyuan 502, which is an improved variety I buy from the input dealer at the township market. My neighbor Lao Wang uses the same seed and his wheat always looks good. Last autumn I put down 100 jin of compound fertilizer as base when I sowed, and this spring I will topdress with another 50 jin of compound plus about 30 jin of urea when the wheat turns green and starts to joint. That is about 75 kg of compound and 15 kg of urea per mu in total. The compound bag says it has nitrogen and phosphate. I will irrigate three times: once now to wake it up from winter, once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling. I spray four times — herbicide once, and then insecticide and fungicide two or three times when the aphids and rust show up. I did rotary tillage before sowing last autumn, so that is already done.

For the summer maize: as soon as the wheat is cut in June, I plant maize without plowing. Everyone here does no-tillage for maize because there is no time between wheat harvest and maize planting. I use Denghai 605, which is a hybrid seed. One package is enough for about one mu, so I buy 8 or 9 packages. I spread about 80 jin of compound fertilizer at planting, and then add another 20 jin of urea when the maize is knee-high. That is about 50 kg of compound and 10 kg of urea per mu. I irrigate twice — once when the heat comes and the seedlings are small, and once when the tassels are out. Three sprays: herbicide once, and insecticide twice for the corn borer. I expect about 1200 jin per mu, same as last year.

For cotton: this is my big crop on 12 mu. I plant Guoxin cotton, an improved variety. I put about 3 jin of seed per mu. In late April I will rotary-till the land and put down 100 jin of compound fertilizer as base. When the plants flower, I topdress with another 80 to 100 jin of compound. Cotton needs a lot of fertilizer, especially potash. Total compound is about 100 kg per mu. I irrigate three times — once at planting if it is dry, once at flowering, and once when the bolls are forming. Cotton needs spraying all summer long. I spray about 14 times — herbicide once at the start, then insecticide every week or two for bollworm and aphids, and fungicide a few times if the weather turns wet. On 12 mu I hire the machine sprayer because my back cannot carry the tank that many times. I expect about 550 jin of seed cotton per mu.

I think about costs every time I open my wallet. A 50 kg bag of compound fertilizer is 130 to 150 yuan now. On 20 mu I spend thousands on inputs. But I would rather put a little too much fertilizer than risk losing yield. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting some fertilizer is just a cost you absorb. My son works in Shijiazhuang and sends money home, so I can afford to buy what I need. I watch what my neighbors do. If everyone is buying the same seed or adding more potash to their cotton, I usually do the same. I am not changing my ways at 63.
